name: core--caddy-edge-stack
description: Caddy edge stack on vm700 replaces the cluster00 ingress layer (Envoy Gateway + ingress-nginx + MetalLB + cert-manager) with one container plus four verbatim nginx sidecars. Written to run in parallel with the cluster so every hostname can be proven before any DNS moves; nothing is cut over by this change

implementation.change: New task file plus templates/caddy/{Caddyfile.j2,10-snippets.caddy.j2,20-public.caddy.j2,30-internal.caddy.j2,40-v2.caddy.j2,docker-compose.yml.j2,env.j2}, the six cluster nginx ConfigMaps extracted verbatim into files/caddy/nginx/, and caddy_* defaults; imported from tasks/main.yaml under tag caddy_stack after the OmniRoute import. Caddy is pulled by digest (ghcr.io/caddybuilds/caddy-cloudflare@sha256:a37a6472f8a47f9bc90b039ec8dec1eacd0115db666556f002662fca3fd8f397), never built, following the OmniRoute precedent. TLS comes from ACME DNS-01 via Cloudflare using the same CERT_MANAGER_CLOUDFLARE_TOKEN the cluster already uses, read from the controller environment with lookup('env') and never copied into this repository. caddy_enabled defaults to false so an unrelated 'make ops' cannot bind :80/:443 on a live host

known_deltas: Rate limiting is dropped for musicengine and omniroute. The live BackendTrafficPolicies set 50 req/s, but Caddy's rate_limit directive comes from mholt/caddy-ratelimit, which the pinned image does not ship. Caddy refuses to load a Caddyfile containing an unknown directive, so keeping it would fail startup for all hostnames, not just those two. Adding the module requires a build, which is forbidden on this host
The HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect stays off in phase 1, mirroring today's behaviour. Enabling it is a separate decision, made after chat and overseerr have been observed on the new stack
HTTP/3 is disabled (protocols h1 h2). The router forwards TCP only, so advertising Alt-Svc would cause clients to attempt H3, stall, and fall back
blocks: shareurl.koeff.com depends on docker.io/bitnami/nginx:1.25.3-debian-11-r6, which now returns HTTP 404 from Docker Hub after Bitnami's 2025 restructuring. The sidecar uses bitnamilegacy/nginx:1.25.3-debian-11-r6 (verified HTTP 200). This is also a live fragility in the cluster today: the running pod survives only on node3's image cache and will not come back from a reschedule
defects_found_and_fixed_during_deploy: docker-compose.yml.j2 mounted the Caddyfile as a second, overlapping bind on top of the read-only /etc/caddy directory mount. Docker cannot create a mountpoint inside a read-only mount, so the caddy container failed to start with 'read-only file system' while all four nginx sidecars came up. Fixed by rendering the Caddyfile into conf.d and mounting that one directory

The role's readiness gate only probed :80, and Caddy binds plain HTTP immediately while ACME is still issuing. The first run therefore reported 'ready' — with a message claiming certificates had been issued — at a moment when :443 completed no TLS handshake at all and every HTTPS request returned 000. Added a second gate that requires a completed TLS handshake, using curl --resolve because SNI is needed and the hostname's public DNS still points at the cluster, plus an explicit fail task so a stuck ACME cannot pass silently

Three variants of the same silent-no-op bug, all found during the Envoy migration. (a) The docker-compose.yml render task was accidentally deleted while editing, so compose read a stale file, recreated nothing, and every task still reported ok while the host kept running the old stack. (b) Compose only recreates a container when its service definition changes, so editing a Caddyfile or snippet left the new config unread on disk — this is what produced a stack that 502'd with a fully green play. Fixed with a graceful 'caddy reload', gated on a config template actually changing so idempotence holds. (c) The same applies to envoy.yaml, which is a bind mount compose does not diff; the sidecar is now restarted when and only when that template changes

Added an 'envoy --mode validate' task in a throwaway container before compose touches the stack. YAML validity does not imply Envoy validity, and a bad config would otherwise stop the old sidecar and crash-loop the new one, taking share.koeff.com and shareurl.koeff.com down until someone read the logs

switchover_readiness.state: prepared, not executed — awaiting the operator's signal
switchover_readiness.scriptable_half: Six *.local.koeff.com A records move 192.168.31.237 -> 192.168.31.152 via the Cloudflare API, using the same token cert-manager and Caddy already use. apply is gated behind a full scripts/migrations/verify_caddy.sh pass and a typed confirmation
switchover_readiness.manual_half: The router's :80/:443 forward must move 192.168.31.235 -> 192.168.31.152. Not reachable from here; apply stops and waits for confirmation rather than pretending otherwise
switchover_readiness.no_change_needed: The seven public hostnames already resolve to the WAN address 151.251.104.115. Only the router decides which internal host that lands on, so their DNS records are not touched
switchover_readiness.rollback: switchover.sh rollback repoints the six records at the cluster and prints the router revert. The cluster is never stopped, so this is a repoint rather than a restore. Cloudflare TTL is auto (300s), so both directions take effect within ~5 minutes
found_while_preparing: shareurl.local.koeff.com -> 192.168.31.235 is an orphan: no HTTPRoute serves it and it returns 000 from the cluster and from Caddy alike. Excluded from the switchover; worth deleting separately
alertmanager/elasticsearch/kibana/local.koeff.com all point at 192.168.31.240, which does not respond to ping. Four stale records, unrelated to this migration
cluster00-node1/2/3.local.koeff.com point at the cluster VMs and will go stale when it is decommissioned

validated_on: vm700 (192.168.31.152), /opt/caddy, Let's Encrypt production. Deployed 2026-08-16 in parallel with cluster00; no DNS changed, no cluster state touched. Verified by scripts/migrations/verify_caddy.sh — 42 passed, 0 failed
not_caused_by_this_change: mpe-api (musicengine.koeff.com backend, port 8770) went down at 21:08:27, four minutes after the Caddy container started at 21:04:21. It was a clean stop (exit 0, not OOM) followed by a rename to mpe-api-srvlocal at 21:08:34 — a deliberate action by something else; this role contains no mpe tasks and ran tag-scoped to caddy_stack. The cluster returns 503 for the same hostname, confirming the backend itself is down rather than the routing. scripts/migrations/verify_caddy.sh was subsequently taught to distinguish a dead upstream (5xx on both paths) from an actual routing divergence, so this cannot masquerade as a migration failure again
